cards.title: ACM SMART CARD
cards.subtitle: Level 1 · The 3 Bs
cards.banner: There is no first aid in a firefight. Win the fight, then provide aid.

blocks.alt: Self aid cycle: 01 minimal self aid, 02 communicate, 03 after the fight. Keep fighting.

items.label: Limb with many wounds
items.text: tourniquet. High and tight, above the wounds.

items.label: Every other wound
items.text: pressure bandage. One per wound.

items.label: Bleeding stopped
items.text: elastic wrap, so wounds do not reopen.
Elastic wrap does not stop a bleeding wound on its own.

rows: Head turn, check pulse, call CLS

blocks.text: Blue skin on the face and arms: short of oxygen. Tell CLS.

items.text: Check the pulse at the neck.
No pulse: CPR for 2 minutes.
Check the pulse again.
Repeat until the pulse returns or CLS takes over.

blocks.text: Weak or missing pulse at the arms or legs: heavy blood loss. Tell CLS.

items.text: Win the fight. Return fire, get to cover, then look at yourself.
Tourniquet any limb with many wounds.
Pressure bandage every other wound.
Elastic wrap once the bleeding has stopped.
Paracetamol for pain. 1 to 2 pills, works in about 4 minutes, lasts about 50.
Call CLS if you cannot stop the bleeding or a limb will not work.
Get back in the fight.
Any unconscious casualty
Any chest wound
Bleeding you cannot stop
A limb that will not work
Win the fight. Do not go to a casualty under fire.
Drag your buddy to cover. Treat behind cover.
Stop the bleeding. Head wounds first, then limbs, then the rest.

items.label: Responsive?
items.text: Yes: finish bandaging, wrap, paracetamol, done. No: call CLS and keep going.

items.label: Breathing?
items.text: No: turn the head to clear the mouth and check again.

items.label: Pulse at the neck?
items.text: No: CPR. Yes: recovery position, stay with them.
Tell CLS what happened, how long they have been down, where the tourniquets are, pulse and breathing, and how many paracetamol.

blocks.text: Airway adjuncts, chest seals, needles, IVs, any medication other than paracetamol.

cards.title: ACM SMART CARD
cards.subtitle: Level 2 · MARCH
cards.banner: Treat in MARCH order. Do not move to the next letter until the current one is controlled.

items.label: Limb, many wounds
items.text: tourniquet.

items.label: Body part, many wounds
items.text: emergency trauma dressing. Not on yourself.

items.label: Single wound
items.text: pressure bandage.

items.label: Once stable
items.text: elastic wrap over bandaged and clotted wounds.

items.label: Bruising, or bleeding that will not stop
items.text: call the Medic for TXA.
Tourniquet off once the wounds under it are bandaged.

rows: NPA or OPA, head-tilt chin-lift, or recovery position
Head turn if mild. Suction bag
Head-tilt chin-lift or recovery position. Medic for i-gel

blocks.text: Suction first. NPA and OPA only go in a clear airway.
With systolic under 90 the reading can be off by up to 30%.

items.text: Fix what you can: tension pneumothorax (seal and decompress), blocked airway (clear it).
Morphine or fentanyl on board: naloxone now.
Connect the AED, select AED mode.
CPR for 2 minutes or until the AED prompts. Let it re-analyze. Repeat.
No AED: CPR for 2 minutes, carotid pulse check, repeat.

items.label: Unconscious, stable vitals
items.text: ammonia inhalant.

items.label: Still unconscious
items.text: go back through M, A, R, C.

items.label: Conscious
items.text: pain, then fractures.

blocks.text: SAM splint, then elastic wrap over it. Significant swelling is a complex fracture: evacuate. Realignment is the Medic's.
IV or IO, fluids, blood, vial medications, i-gel, surgical airway, thoracostomy, manual AED, fracture realignment, casualty conversion.

rows: Moderate to severe pain, short term
Not with chest injury, slow breathing, low blood volume or altered mental status
Opioids last longer. Watch and re-dose
Lowers heart rate and blood pressure

cards.title: ACM SMART CARD
cards.subtitle: Level 3 · MARCH · Card 1 of 2
cards.banner: Everything CLS does, plus anything that needs a vein, a scalpel or a rhythm decision.

items.label: TXA 1 g IV
items.text: for severe bleeding, noticeable bruising or a bleeding hemothorax.
Bruising with a falling blood pressure is internal bleeding. TXA and fluids.
Clots are unstable. Wrap or stitch once stable.

rows: Open airway, collapse. Airway must be clear first

blocks.text: Use the least invasive airway that solves the problem.

items.label: Stethoscope
items.text: muffled on one side is a pneumothorax.

items.label: Tension pneumothorax
items.text: chest seal plus NCD, or thoracostomy.

items.label: Hemothorax
items.text: TXA, then thoracostomy and chest tube.
Consider lidocaine IM before thoracostomy.

blocks.label: Chest tube
blocks.text: drain with the ACCUVAC or a suction bag, re-drain until no blood comes out, close the incision.

items.label: Unconscious, stable vitals
items.text: ammonia inhalant.

items.label: Still unconscious
items.text: go back through M, A, R, C.

items.label: Fracture
items.text: lidocaine 50 to 100 mg IM, realign, SAM splint, check mobility, wrap.

items.label: Complex fracture
items.text: evacuate.

blocks.text: Crashing casualty: IO first, then move the bags to an IV. Tourniquets block IVs on that limb.

items.text: Check the blood type on the dog tag. A mismatch can kill.
O- goes to anyone. AB+ receives from anyone. A negative recipient only takes negative blood.

items.label: Calcium chloride 1 g IV
items.text: after the first unit (500 ml), then after every 4 units. Never IM.
Connect the kit to the donor's IV. It does not work on an IO.
Wait for it to fill.
Disconnect and use it as fresh whole blood, soon.
Casualty unconscious, alive and not bleeding externally.
If the mission requires it: in a medical facility or vehicle, and ertapenem 1 g given.
Keep treating the AI casualty until it is evacuated.

blocks.text: Confirm with a carotid pulse check. Fix the reversible cause. Then rhythm, drug, shock, CPR.

rows: Check for terminal injuries, epinephrine, CPR

blocks.text: PEA looks like sinus on the EKG. Always confirm with a pulse check.

items.label: Epinephrine 1 mg IV.
items.text: The only drug that helps in asystole.

items.label: Amiodarone 300 mg IV
items.text: for VT or VF. Two vials. Less does nothing.

items.label: Lidocaine 100 mg IV
items.text: for VT or VF. One vial.
Never amiodarone and lidocaine together. Leave 5 to 10 minutes between them, and between amiodarone doses.
2 minutes, or until the AED prompts. Re-analyze. Repeat.

items.label: Short of oxygen, one medic or no i-gel
items.text: 30 compressions, then 2 BVM breaths.

items.label: Short of oxygen, two medics and an i-gel
items.text: continuous CPR and BVM.

items.label: Pulse is back
items.text: EtCO2 jumps to 40 to 50, cyanosis fades, carotid pulse returns.

cards.title: ACM SMART CARD
cards.subtitle: Level 3 · Card 2 of 2
cards.banner: Draw = dose ÷ concentration. IV drugs need an IV or IO first. More than the range adds side effects, not benefit.

rows: After the first unit of blood, then every 4 units
4 mg IV or IM, max 8 mg
Wound infection, before conversion if required
2 mg IV or IM, 2 to 4 mg to start

items.text: No amiodarone and lidocaine within 5 to 10 minutes of each other. No second amiodarone within 5 to 10 minutes.
No opioids with low blood volume, slow heart rate, slow breathing, chest injury or altered mental status.
Naloxone for any arrest with opioids on board.
Calcium chloride never IM, and not in ventricular fibrillation.
No epinephrine with a very fast heart rate or high blood pressure.
No esmolol, adenosine, amiodarone or midazolam with a slow heart rate.
Morphine autoinjector is not issued.
